title: Playing with his sons on television
summary: Steven and Ted Jr. say they owe their playing to their father, who hired them, and Hinton calls Wilson exacting.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, it's a party. You know, one of the nicest things that happened to me recently was on television one day, that television show with you and your two sons playing on that program. I tell you, it put me on cloud nine just to see you. Steven and Teddy, how did you feel about that show? Playing with your Dad?
I thought it was an invaluable experience. And I felt very fortunate to be able to have the chance.

Well, for me, any ability I have to perform is exclusively because of Dad. It also gave me the ability to put together the jazz history courses, because I didn't even have to read about it because I heard it and saw it and could go back to it in retrospect. But the confidence in being a performer and also my own sort of like change in plans in taking on the bass fiddle, all that was due solely to the inspiration of Dad. He was the only person, also, to give me the opportunity to do it. He was the only one who hired me.
He's a mean dude, though when it comes to music. You either do it right or you get off.
Well, we all know when something is right and when it's not.
But you're one of them kind of cats, when you get in the car, you take off. Shame all of them.
Oh, get out of here, Teddy.
That's what makes you play -- and my ability is due exclusively to Dad.
